title: The false myth of the surge in Italian self-citations, and the positive effect of bibliometric evaluations on the increase of the impact of Italian research
reasoning: The paper discusses issues of academic integrity related to self-citation and the impact of bibliometric evaluations on research impact. While it touches upon what might be considered 'unethical' citation practices ('citation gaming', 'rigging the system'), it does not evaluate or benchmark religion, morals, or ethics as a core component of its analysis. It is an empirical study of citation patterns and their effects on research rankings, rather than a normative ethical inquiry.
